3. FALSE — ARM7 uses a 3-stage pipeline (ARM9 moved to 5 stages).
5. FALSE — a branch writes the target address into the PC.

1. Thumb benefit: 16-bit Thumb instructions roughly halve code size, so the firmware fits smaller/cheaper flash and makes better use of memory bandwidth — ideal for a memory-constrained embedded sensor device.

2. Instruction execution: handled by the datapath under the Control Unit — the CU decodes each instruction and drives the ALU/registers; the ALU performs the actual arithmetic/logical operations, and the CPSR records the resulting flags.

3. Data hazards: in the 3-stage pipeline an instruction may read a register before a previous instruction has written its result (RAW hazard), producing wrong values or stalls. Mitigation: insert NOPs/reorder instructions (software scheduling), since ARM7 has no forwarding; the compiler's instruction scheduler usually does this.
